title: SoftWater: The 2-Bit Model With an fp16 Head Isn't 2-Bit
hook: In small LLMs with modern vocabularies, the output head holds 15–30% of all parameters. Leave it in fp16 and your '2-bit' model quietly stores several times as many bits per weight.
key_points: Post-training quantization pipelines routinely skip the softmax output layer — but the head is 15–30% of parameters in small LLMs with large vocabularies.

A second-order analysis gives a class-aware geometry: error is weighted by both feature covariance and per-class softmax curvature.
SoftWater spends fine grids on frequent, low-variance classes and coarse grids on rare ones — a big win under Zipfian token distributions.

content_html: Quantization papers usually leave the softmax output layer alone. Joao V. Cavalcanti and Ashia C. Wilson (arXiv, August 2026) point out how much that costs: in small LLMs with modern vocabularies, the head holds 15–30% of all parameters, so a nominal "2-bit" model with an fp16 head stores several times as many bits per weight as advertised.
extra_html:
The method

They pose head quantization as a rate-distortion problem under the KL divergence between the original and quantized output distributions — the right target for a layer whose job is producing a distribution. A second-order analysis reveals a class-aware geometry: quantization error is weighted jointly by feature covariance and class-specific softmax curvature. A separability approximation replaces the full Kn×Kn Cholesky with one n×n factorization rescaled per class, so the lattice can be encoded with successive interference cancellation and both statistics come from a single forward pass.

The result, SoftWater, gives fine grids to frequent, low-variance classes and coarse ones to rare classes — which matters a lot under Zipfian token distributions.

Results

Across five models from 1B to 32B, SoftWater beats the released WaterSIC quantizer at matched head rates on 59 of 60 test points, cutting head-induced KL by 6.5x–8.3x at 2 bits without any of that pipeline's refinements. On Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct with a quantized body, a 2-bit head removes 45–60% of stored bytes for a 2.9–3.7% perplexity increase; on a tied model, a 4-bit head is near-lossless. One practical caveat the authors flag: the class-side statistic comes from calibration data, so matching calibration to the deployment domain gives the lowest KL there.

flashcards.prompt: Why does leaving the softmax head in fp16 undercut a '2-bit' small LLM?

choices.text: The head can be 15–30% of all parameters, so its high-precision weights dominate the average bits per weight
The head is recomputed at every decoding step, so precision costs compute not memory
fp16 heads force the rest of the model back to fp16 at inference

flashcards.explanation_html: With modern large vocabularies the output head is a big share of parameters; an fp16 head plus a 2-bit body stores several times more bits per weight than the nominal rate.

flashcards.prompt: What objective does SoftWater optimize instead of weight-space error?
flashcards.back_html: Rate-distortion under the KL divergence between the original and quantized output distributions — matching what the head is actually for.
Giving fine quantization grids to frequent, low-variance classes and coarse grids to rare ones, since second-order error is weighted by feature covariance and per-class softmax curvature.
